text:
Taylor: Dropping a quick iteration: make the time range selector stick once you scroll past the header. primary goal: keep context for p95/heatmap comparisons while you scrub. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/sticky-range-v2

Sofia: I like that. couple things: on narrow sizes the sticky bar eats vertical real estate and the scrubber’s drag handle gets crowded. could we collapse the sampling chip into an overflow menu on < 960px?

Ravi: collapsing makes sense. alternative: compact chip with icon + number (e.g., "S x100") to save width. also concern about visual stability when sticky toggles mid-scroll; layout shifts feel janky. we should animate height change or pre-allocate space.

Elena: accessibility notes: ensure focus order doesn't jump when the clone becomes sticky. if we duplicate controls for visual sticky, add aria-hidden="true" on the clone that isn't interactive. also add a skip-link at the top of the sticky region: "Skip to heatmap".

A11yBot: contrast check: compact chip color #0A84FF on white has 4.5:1 at 12px? borderline for AA. Recommend white text on #0A84FF at 14px or dark text on #E6F2FF background. Also flag: motion during stick should respect prefers-reduced-motion.

Taylor: good catch. I'll try white text on #0A84FF. For motion we can use a subtle translateY with reduced-motion fallback. small CSS example:
```
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .sticky { transition: none; }
}
```

Sofia: about tooltip behavior: p95 tooltips sometimes overlap the sticky bar. propose rules: 1) if tooltip would intersect sticky, render above sticky with pointer, 2) if there's no room, float inside an overlay that spans the sticky bar area. also we should test with long series names that wrap.

Ravi: linking tooltip rules to z-index is brittle across browsers. I'd prefer nudging the chart up by stickyHeight (configurable) so tooltips stay within chart canvas. downside: consumes vertical space though. Maybe make nudging opt-in per user preference.

Elena: microcopy nit: change "Sampling: 1/100" to "Sampled: 1 in 100 requests" for clarity in assistive speech and non-native readers. shorter compact form can be "S:1/100" in the collapsed chip. Also ensure the dynamic announcement uses polite aria-live.

Taylor: action list: 1) I'll push two Figma variants (compact-collapse vs nudge-chart). 2) I'll update chip color + copy. 3) add prefers-reduced-motion CSS. 4) include aria-hidden duplicate pattern. @Sofia can you run responsive keyboard flows on both variants? @Ravi can prototype the chart-nudge vs tooltip-reposition logic in playground? @Elena can run a screen reader sweep with the new copy?

Sofia: yep, I'll run keyboard/responsive today and post results here.

Ravi: prototyping tooltip + nudge in the playground by EOD, will post a short clip.

Elena: I'll test VoiceOver/JAWS tomorrow morning and report accessibility readouts.

A11yBot: re-check scheduled after changes: run contrast and landmark tests. also run automated ARIA validator on the duplicated controls approach.

Taylor: thanks all. keeping thread as canonical for this iteration. I'll open a tiny PR for the chip color + copy after Figma updates.

Sofia: :thumbsup:

Ravi: :ok_hand:

Elena: thanks!
